entry.title: Flash Memory Explained: NAND vs NOR, Architecture, and Memory Organization
entry.summary: Flash memory is a type of non-volatile semiconductor memory that can be electrically erased and reprogrammed. It is based on floating-gate MOSFETs (Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors) where data is stored by trapping electrons in a floating gate, altering the threshold voltage of the transistor to represent binary states. Unlike volatile memory like DRAM, flash retains data even when power is removed, making it ideal for applications requiring persistent storage such as SSDs, USB drives, memory cards and embedded systems. Flash memory evolved from EEPROM, but instead of erasing individual bytes, it erases data in larger blocks, which significantly improves speed, density, and cost efficiency.
